content: The live smoke test this task asked for immediately surfaced a real bug: the gRPC gateway failed at 30s, and it turned out Runtime's own direct /chat endpoint did too -- the earlier session's belief that 'it runs' did not hold up under a fresh AppHost start. Root-caused to the global ConfigureHttpClientDefaults resilience default applying to every HttpClient including the new gRPC channel, and found that the earlier per-client override in Runtime/Program.cs had never actually taken effect (dead code sitting on disk since an earlier trail). Fixed at the shared ServiceDefaults registration site and verified with three separate live, successful, Ollama-generated responses after restarting the AppHost. This is exactly the value a live smoke test provides over code review alone. Filed a next_seed for the still-unused Pmcro__* env vars AppHost already passes to both projects.

next_seed.summary: AppHost passes Pmcro__RuntimeRoot/TrailRoot/QueueRoot/SkillsRoot as environment variables into both ProjectName.Runtime and ProjectName.OrchestrationApi, but neither Program.cs reads them yet -- decide what they're actually meant to enable (e.g. the runtime querying its own trail/queue state) and wire it up, or remove them from AppHost.cs if they were provisional and are not needed.
